A whole programme that does not fit is passed over

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004539
Type formula assumption
has description in the module When a programme's cost exceeds the budget left, the fill passes over it and tests the next, which agrees with the article's step 3, where neither Q nor R fits after P. The pass-over is the convention of this package; none of the cited sources states which variant a league table of whole programmes uses. Stopping at the first programme that does not fit is the other convention and can buy less health (HE-EX-CELT-009). A programme whose cost equals the budget left fits, since the test is at most B.
has module record identifier HE-AS-CELT-007
has title in the module A whole programme that does not fit is passed over

isDefinedBy hemo-formulae.owlexternal

Additive shift on imputed QALYs of those lost to follow-up

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004792
Type formula assumption
has description in the module The shift is an offset added to the QALYs of those lost, the delta parameter of the pattern-mixture approach that Leurent and colleagues describe, applied after imputation under missing at random. Because a fraction p of an arm is shifted by delta, the arm mean moves by p times delta in every imputed dataset, and Rubin's rules average the point estimates, so the pooled QALY gain moves by the same amount (derived). With covariates in the imputation model the base-case gain is the multiple imputation estimate, which can differ from the difference in observed means; the article's example takes the two to be equal.
has module record identifier HE-AS-LTFU-001
has title in the module Additive shift on imputed QALYs of those lost to follow-up
has title key additive-shift-on-imputed-qalys-of-those-lost-to-follow-up
isDefinedBy hemo-formulae.owlexternal

Assumption of AIC, AIC differences and Akaike weights for candidate survival curves

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004830
Type formula assumption
has description in the module All candidates are fitted by maximum likelihood to identical data, and the set is specified before fitting. The weights are conditional on the set: adding or removing a model changes every weight. Subtracting the minimum before exponentiating also avoids exponentials of large negative numbers, which underflow to zero in floating-point arithmetic when AIC values run into the thousands.

Assumption of Annual event rate to a model-cycle transition probability

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004864
Type formula assumption
has description in the module The event rate is constant across the year, so every cycle within the year has the same probability, and a month counts as one twelfth of a year. Where the rate changes with age or time since treatment, the function is applied cycle by cycle with the rate for that period.

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004873
Type formula assumption
has description in the module The annual probability arises from a constant rate within the year, and only one event leads out of the starting state. With competing exits the cause-specific rates are separated first, as in HE-FM-TP-004.

Assumption of Antithetic pairs of exponential survival times with a pair-mean standard error

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004931
Type formula assumption
has description in the module Survival times are exponential with a constant hazard and are sampled by the inverse distribution function, so U and 1-U give mirrored quantiles. Each patient has its own random number, used for the same purpose in both runs. Survival time falls as U rises, so it is monotone in U and the within-pair correlation is negative.

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004905
Type formula assumption
has description in the module Utilities share a common variance at every visit, the correlation depends only on elapsed time, and patients are independent with complete utility data. The standard error assumes equal variances and equal arm sizes, as in the article's example. phi has to be above zero because elapsed times can be fractions of a year.

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004880
Type formula assumption
has description in the module Everyone in a subgroup is given the subgroup's mean health, so inequality within subgroups is ignored and only variation between the subgroups that define unfair inequality counts. Shares sum to 1 after normalisation.

has description in the module The survey prevalences and their ratio hold in the local population, the ratio is causal and unconfounded, and each prevalent case costs the same in both groups. The result is an annual cost of prevalent cases, not a lifetime cost of new cases.

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7005199
Type formula assumption
has description in the module No tied standardised effects or tied variances, so the null variance needs no tie correction; a tied pair counts as neither concordant nor discordant, and with ties the variance is only approximate. With fewer than 10 studies, or studies of similar size, the Cochrane Handbook advises against tests for funnel plot asymmetry; it does not name the rank correlation test, so applying this to the Begg test is an inference.

Working from the differences rather than the raw BIC values keeps the exponentials within floating-point range when BIC values run into the thousands.

Type formula assumption
has description in the module The replicates come from resampling that copies the trial design, and the statistic behaves like an average, so a normal interval is a reasonable first summary. Efron and Tibshirani note that this standard interval is sometimes good and sometimes not, and it does not suit the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio, whose variance may be undefined.

With continuous risks every patient forms a group of one, the resolution term then equals the uncertainty term and the partition says nothing useful, so continuous risks are binned before the partition is read, and the bins are reported.

Type formula assumption
has description in the module K is computed at the disease-free state and is non-negative, so its spectral radius is a real eigenvalue with a non-negative eigenvector. Power iteration on K settles when that eigenvalue is strictly larger in modulus than all others. A host and vector matrix with a zero diagonal has eigenvalues R_0 and minus R_0, so the one-generation ratio swings, and the two-generation ratio, or iteration on K plus the identity matrix as in the Excel version, is used instead. Three generations in the calculator line give an approximation, while the R and Python routines are exact to rounding.

has description in the module Costs and QALYs are expected values per person on one basis. Equal cost with more QALYs, or equal QALYs at lower cost, counts as dominance (HE-AS-DOM-001). https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7005699
Type formula assumption
has description in the module Where two strategies tie for the highest net monetary benefit at a grid value, the R and Python versions keep the one with more QALYs, so an equal-cost strategy with fewer QALYs is not reported at a value of zero. The Excel version takes the first maximum, so dominated strategies, ties included, are screened out first with HE-IM-DOM-002. A strategy lying exactly on a segment ties with its neighbours at one value only, so whether it is reported depends on rounding in floating point (with QALYs of 1.0, 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 at costs of 1,000 to 4,000 the second strategy is reported and the third is not), where the elimination function HE-CF-CEF-001 keeps both. has description in the module As in HE-AS-MECH-005 to HE-AS-MECH-007, with S(q) = a q minus b q^2 / 2, a above theta_H and nu at least 0 and below 1, except that U_0 may be positive. Assumption of Computational function for the stop or continue decision at one interim look of a two-arm trial

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7005771
Type formula assumption
has description in the module The prior and the pair observations are normal with known variance, outcomes are observed at once, there is no discounting and no switching cost. Fixed costs are treated as committed, as Forster and colleagues assume for ProFHER once the trial was commissioned, so only the remaining pairs and any further analysis are costed. The participant in each remaining pair on the arm expected to be inferior forgoes abs(mu_t), the participants' loss of HE-FM-ENBS-002 valued on the interim evidence; that valuation at an interim look is this package's application, since Fenwick and colleagues and Flight and colleagues value the loss on the information held before the study, and Flight and colleagues set it equal to the signed prior incremental net benefit, which equals its absolute value when that benefit is positive. Flight and colleagues note that the loss holds only if the new intervention cannot be used in practice before the trial ends and may be zero if it is potentially cost-effective and can be used while research is ongoing. It replaces the online learning term of HE-FM-AVOI-001 and is not added to it. A net gain of exactly zero gives go of 0, the strict inequality of the KG* rule. The check is one-stage, so a decision to continue also holds for the optimal sequential policy, while a decision to stop may come too early (HE-FM-AVOI-001).

Constant recovery rate implying an exponential infectious period

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004347
Type formula assumption
has description in the module A constant recovery rate gamma means the time infectious is exponentially distributed with mean 1/gamma, so D is a mean and individual durations vary. The probability of recovering within a model cycle of length t is 1 minus exp(minus gamma t) by the rate conversion of HE-FN-TP-001, not gamma times t. Beta and gamma are in the same time unit, so their ratio has none, and Delamater and colleagues describe R_0 as cases per case, not a rate.

Factor-neutral schooling effect and a suppressed intercept in gross investment

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004673
Type formula assumption
has description in the module One more year of E raises the marginal products of M and TH by the same percentage, Grossman's Hicks or factor-neutrality assumption, so schooling changes the gross investment obtained from given inputs but gives no reason to change the ratio of care to time. Grossman writes the estimating form with its intercept suppressed, left out of the equation as shown, so the level of the efficiency factor is not pinned down. Because health capital is measured in abstract units, the formula absorbs the intercept by counting E from the level at which the factor is 1 (a normalisation made here), so only differences in E between people or years carry meaning. Allocative efficiency, in which schooling improves knowledge of the true effects of inputs and so the choice of inputs, is a separate channel that this formula leaves out.

Section 13.11 defines a cost of living index by the minimum cost of reaching base-period utility, states that because of this stress on minimum cost it will usually give a lower rate of inflation, and describes consumers switching towards goods and services that are becoming relatively cheaper.

has description in the module M is chosen and justified before the data are seen, as CPMP/EWP/482/99 section III and the EMEA 2005 margin guideline section 2 require, because a margin chosen after the results can always be made to give non-inferiority. ICH E10 section 1.5.1.1 states that the margin cannot be greater than the smallest effect the active control would reliably be expected to have against placebo in the planned trial, and the FDA guidance sets M2, the largest clinically acceptable loss, at or below M1. https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/hemo/HEMO_7004379
Type formula assumption
has description in the module K is computed with everyone susceptible, so each entry is an expected count of new cases over the whole infectious period of one case and is zero or above; van den Driessche notes that F is entrywise non-negative and V a non-singular M-matrix, so the inverse of V and K are non-negative. Columns index the group of the infector and rows the group of the new case, as in the definition of Diekmann, Heesterbeek and Roberts. A transposed matrix has the same eigenvalues and so the same R_0, but its dominant eigenvector, the distribution of cases over groups, differs.

has description in the module Each pair's incremental net monetary benefit is normal with known variance and the prior is normal, so the interim posterior is normal with mean mu_t and effective sample size n_t (equations 2 and 3 of Chick and colleagues), and the posterior mean after m more pairs is normal about mu_t with variance sigma_X squared over n_t times m over n_t plus m (their equation 6). That holds for a shift confined to the new treatment arm whenever anyone in that arm is lost, and for a common shift only when the new treatment arm loses the larger share.
